verdict.summary: You can create one Production OAuth app for real users and connect many customers. Calendly does not document a provider app-review step or review wait. The main technical work is OAuth security: PKCE, a code-exchange safeguard, and refresh-token rotation.
verdict.activeEffort: 2–4 hours (estimate), mostly building secure OAuth token handling
verdict.mainGate: Every OAuth connection must use PKCE. When refreshing tokens, store the replacement refresh token because the old token is revoked.

recommendation.text: Use a standard Production OAuth app for the REST API. Use one stable callback URL. Create a separate Sandbox app for development. This supports many customers without using personal access tokens.

sources.quote: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while personal access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.
We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

scopeTiers.text: Read a customer's profile and scheduled events. This causes normal user consent only.

sources.quote: For newly created OAuth apps and new Personal Access Tokens, no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.
Retrieve scheduled events and event invitee information.

scopeTiers.need: Read the user's profile, event types, and scheduled events.

scopeTiers.text: Read availability for scheduling suggestions. This adds availability data to the consent screen.

sources.quote: Overly broad scopes can lead to unnecessary user friction at install time.

scopeTiers.need: Suggest times using the user's availability.

scopeTiers.text: Book, cancel, or mark meetings as no-show. This asks users to grant write access.

sources.quote: Create event invitees, cancel events or mark invitees as no-show.
A :write scope implicitly includes the corresponding :read scope within the same domain.

scopeTiers.need: Take explicit scheduling actions for the user.

scopeTiers.text: Receive near real-time changes. This needs webhook permission and related read access.

sources.quote: Webhook subscriptions must be scoped by the event family you want to receive. Your app must be granted the related read scopes to receive webhook event payloads.
Recommended for near real time updates. Not required if the integration relies on polling.

scopeTiers.need: Keep scheduled-event data current without frequent polling.

essentials.text: Access tokens expire after 2 hours. Keep refresh tokens only on your server. Refresh tokens are single-use, so atomically save the returned replacement token.

sources.quote: Access Tokens expire after 2 hours.
A refresh token is revoked immediately after a successful POST /oauth/token call.
Refresh tokens are handled only on the server side , in secure storage.

essentials.text: Configure exactly one callback URL. Sandbox accepts HTTPS and localhost HTTP. Production accepts HTTPS only.

sources.quote: Redirect URI : the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
Sandbox https URIs, and http URIs on localhost . Example: http://localhost:1234/callback
Production https URIs only

essentials.text: Use a free Calendly account with a Sandbox app for development. No OAuth test-user cap is published.

sources.quote: Environment type : select Sandbox for development and testing, or Production when your app is ready for real users.
Webhooks and the Scheduling API are also available on all Calendly plans, including Free.

essentials.text: Queue requests separately for each connected user. Paid users allow 500 requests per minute. Free users allow 50. OAuth token requests allow 8 per user per minute.

sources.quote: Paid Plans 500 requests per user per minute
Free Plan 50 requests per user per minute
Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.

essentials.text: No developer registration fee is documented. API access works for connected users on any Calendly plan. Some product features remain plan-gated.

sources.quote: Developers can make GET and POST requests to API endpoints on behalf of a Calendly user on any subscription plan.
The following API endpoints are available only on the Enterprise plan:

essentials.text: Create a separate Production OAuth app when ready for real customer data. Production callbacks must use HTTPS.

sources.quote: Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
Production https URIs only

essentials.text: No OAuth app review or launch approval is documented. Create the Production app directly and rely on user consent.

sources.quote: Create an OAuth app to access Calendly data on behalf of other Calendly users.

essentials.text: Use PKCE with S256 for every OAuth connection. Verify webhook signatures using HMAC SHA-256. Get legal approval before sharing Calendly data with an LLM provider.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use PKCE conforming to RFC 7636, with the `S256` method.
When you create an OAuth 2.0 app, a webhook signing key will automatically be generated for all webhooks related to your application.
Use of customer data must be transparent by disclosing the collection, use and sharing of the data. You must limit your use of the data to the practices you disclose.
prior written consent.

requests.text: Generate CODE_CHALLENGE from CODE_VERIFIER with SHA-256; PKCE is required.

sources.quote:
https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID 
 & response_type= code 
 & redirect_uri= REDIRECT_URI 
 & code_challenge_method= S256 
 & code_challenge= CODE_CHALLENGE
Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method. If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Use the same redirect URI used to obtain the authorization code.

sources.quote: Send a POST request to Get Access Token at https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token . Include these parameters:

grant_type : authorization_code 
 code : the authorization code
 redirect_uri : the same redirect URI that you used to get the code
 client_id : your client ID
 code_verifier : the verifier that you generated in step 1
If your app runs on a server, also send your client secret. Use HTTP Basic authentication with your client ID as the username and your client secret as the password.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: Refresh tokens are single-use, so immediately store the new refresh_token returned by a successful response.

sources.quote: The main change is in how refresh tokens behave when you call the POST /oauth/token endpoint.
Each successful response from POST /oauth/token will still return a new access token and a new refresh token .

detail.text: Log in or sign up for Calendly. You need this account to create and manage OAuth apps.

sources.quote: Log in to Calendly, or sign up for a Calendly account.

steps.title: Choose the minimum scopes

detail.text: Start with read scopes for the first release. Add write scopes only for visible features that users explicitly enable. This reduces consent friction.

sources.quote: Overly broad scopes can lead to unnecessary user friction at install time.

steps.output:
Scope request:
- users:read
- event_types:read
- scheduled_events:read
Add availability:read only for time suggestions.
Add scheduled_events:write only after users enable booking actions.
Ask for webhooks:write only for push updates.

detail.text: Open Calendly Developer tools and create a Sandbox OAuth app. Enter one HTTPS callback URL or a localhost HTTP callback. Save the client secret and webhook signing key immediately.

sources.quote: You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.
Enter exactly one URI.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth callback

detail.text: Build the callback handler around a one-time signed state value. Bind it to the user's session and PKCE verifier. Calendly does not document a state parameter, so your app must protect the connection flow itself.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use PKCE conforming to RFC 7636, with the `S256` method.
### Query parameters

steps.output:
On connect, create a one-time signed state record.
Store user ID, return path, PKCE verifier, and expiry.
Send S256 code_challenge to /oauth/authorize.
On callback, verify state and exact callback URL.
Exchange code with the stored verifier.
Encrypt tokens server-side.
Atomically replace refresh tokens after every refresh.

steps.title: Add webhook verification

detail.text: Verify each webhook before processing it. Use the raw request body and reject old timestamps. This prevents forged or replayed deliveries.

sources.quote: you can use to reject the webhook if the timestamp in the signature header is too old based on the tolerance zone.

steps.output:
Verify Calendly-Webhook-Signature before processing.
Compute HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`.
Compare signatures with a constant-time check.
Reject stale timestamps.
Store delivery IDs before applying changes.

detail.text: Run the authorization flow against the Sandbox app. Confirm the callback exchanges the code using its matching PKCE verifier. Test a failed refresh by clearing the connection and reconnecting.

sources.quote: For the authorization_code grant, include the code_verifier that matches the code_challenge you sent to the authorization endpoint.
On refresh failure (e.g., 400/401), you clear tokens and ask the user to re-authorize instead of retrying endlessly.

detail.text: Use per-user queues and backoff for 429 responses. Test token refreshes without exceeding the OAuth token limit. Test scheduling actions against the connected user's plan limits.

sources.quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.
5 requests per user per day

detail.text: Publish a privacy notice before enabling connections. Explain what Calendly data you collect, why you use it, and whether an LLM provider receives it. Obtain required written consent for third-party processing.

gotchas.text: Do not use personal access tokens for customer connections. They are for one company's internal or private application.

sources.quote: If you need to securely share data from your or your company’s Calendly account with an internal or private application that’s not for use by others outside of your company, then use personal access tokens.

gotchas.text: A refresh token becomes unusable immediately after a successful refresh. Parallel refresh requests can disconnect a customer.

sources.quote: A refresh token is revoked immediately after a successful POST /oauth/token call.

gotchas.text: One OAuth app accepts exactly one callback URL. Do not create a callback URL for each customer's account.

sources.quote: Enter exactly one URI.

gotchas.text: Booking limits depend on each connected user's plan. Free and Trial users can make only 5 invitee requests daily.

sources.quote: 5 requests per user per day

gotchas.text: Enterprise-only endpoints and organization-wide actions may fail for ordinary users. Organization-wide actions require an Admin or Owner token.

sources.quote: Admin/Owner role: Tokens generated by an admin or owner provide broader access.
